newsitem.title: USA: PSA lauds Moynihan's delay of stadium bill date.
newsitem.headline: PSA lauds Moynihan's delay of stadium bill date.

text.p: A Public Securities Association official said Monday he is "very pleased" with Sen. Daniel Patrick Moynihan's announcement on Friday that he will delay the effective date of his stadium financing bill.

"The action he took Friday should give market participants the ability to complete pending financing activity that has been hamstrung by the earlier 'date-of-introduction' effective date," Micah Green, executive vice president of the PSA said in a written statement.

Moynihan, a Democrat from New York, announced on Friday that when he reintroduces S. 1880, the Stop Tax-exempt Arena Debt Issuance Act, in the 105th Congress, the effective date will be the date that a congressional committee actually acts on the bill.
The stadiums bill introduced by Moynihan on June 14, 1996, had a June 14, 1996, which opponents charged is chilling the market for stadium financings even though no action has been taken on the bill.

"While we continue to oppose any new limits on state and local financing decisions, Senator Monihan's intention to reintroduce the bill with a (new) effective date will allow a more substantive debate without the chilling effects of S. 1880," Green said.
